title: Apple design
sourceNote: apple-design skill, from Apple WWDC talks
summary: Fluid interfaces: immediate, interruptible, and physical.

overview.purpose: Make a web interface feel like an extension of the hand, the way Apple's do.
overview.when: Building or reviewing gestures, springs, sheets, materials, or type.
takeaways: Hand the spring the finger's velocity
Critically damped unless a flick earned the bounce

sections.title: Response
sections.intro: The moment lag appears, directness falls off a cliff.

items.title: Pointer down
items.text: Highlight on press, not on release.

items.title: Continuous
items.text: Feedback tracks the pointer the whole way through.

items.title: No extra wait
items.text: Drop debounces and artificial delays on the input path.

items.title: One to one
items.text: The element stays glued to the finger.

items.title: Grab offset
items.text: Respect where they grabbed, not the center.

items.title: Pointer capture
items.text: Tracking continues after the pointer leaves the element.

sections.title: Interruptibility
sections.intro: The thought and the gesture happen in parallel.

items.title: Live value
items.text: Start from the on-screen transform, never the target.

items.title: No lockout
items.text: A moving element can be grabbed mid-flight.

items.title: Carry velocity
items.text: Re-target without cutting the speed to zero.

items.title: Separate axes
items.text: Spring X and Y on their own.

sections.title: Springs
sections.intro: A spring is a conversation, not a fixed duration.

items.title: Damping
items.text: 1.0 settles with no bounce. Lower overshoots.

items.title: Response
items.text: How fast it arrives, in seconds. Not a duration.

items.title: Default
items.text: Critically damped for chrome.

items.title: Momentum only
items.text: Damping around 0.8 only after a flick.
items.more: Overshoot on a menu that faded in feels wrong. Overshoot on a card you flicked feels right.

items.title: Shipped values
items.text: Move 1.0 / 0.4. Rotation 0.8 / 0.4. Sheet 0.8 / 0.3.

sections.title: Momentum
sections.intro: The animation continues at the finger's speed.

items.title: Velocity handoff
items.text: Pass the release velocity into the spring.

items.title: Relative velocity
items.text: Divide by the distance still left, when the API wants it normalized.
items.more: relativeVelocity = gestureVelocity / (target − current). Motion takes raw px/s.

items.title: Projection
items.text: Land where the flick is going, not where it let go.
items.more: project(v) = (v / 1000) * d / (1 − d), with d ≈ 0.998. Snap to the point nearest that projection, then hand off the velocity.

items.title: Direction
items.text: Use the sign of the velocity to commit or reverse.

sections.title: Space
sections.intro: If something leaves one way, it should return the same way.

items.title: Same path
items.text: A panel from the right dismisses to the right.

items.title: Anchor
items.text: Menus grow from the control that opened them.

items.title: Hint
items.text: The in-between frames point at the outcome.

items.title: Rubber band
items.text: Edges resist. They do not stop hard.

sections.title: Gestures
sections.intro: Feel lives in the first frames of a tap or a drag.

items.title: Tap
items.text: Highlight down, commit up, and allow a cancel by dragging away.
items.more: About 10px of slop around the target.

items.title: Drag
items.text: A small threshold, then track one to one.

items.title: In parallel
items.text: Recognize the candidates together, then drop the losers.

items.title: Frames
items.text: Animate transform and opacity, on the display clock.

sections.title: Materials
sections.intro: Translucency is a floating layer, not a solid bar.

items.title: Chrome
items.text: Bars blur. Content scrolls underneath.

items.title: Weight
items.text: Heavier materials for structure, lighter for controls.
items.more: Never stack a light translucent surface on another.

items.title: Focus
items.text: Dim and push back for a modal. No scrim for a side panel.

items.title: Vibrancy
items.text: Heavier, higher-contrast type over a blur.

items.title: Materialize
items.text: Animate blur and scale together, not opacity alone.

sections.title: Sound and haptics
sections.intro: Motion, sound, and haptics fire on the same frame.

items.title: Causality
items.text: Trigger feedback on the event that caused it.

items.title: Harmony
items.text: Visual, sound, and haptic share one frame.

items.title: Utility
items.text: Reserve it for commit, snap, success, or error.

items.title: Motion
items.text: Cross-fade instead of a slide or a spring.

items.title: Transparency
items.text: Solid surfaces, and drop the blur.

items.title: Contrast
items.text: A near-solid fill and a real border.

sections.title: Type
sections.intro: Tracking and leading change with the size.

items.title: Tracking
items.text: Negative on large type. Near zero on body.

items.title: Leading
items.text: Tight headings, looser body.

items.title: Hierarchy
items.text: Weight, size, and leading as one set.

items.title: System font
items.text: Start there, and scale spacing with the text.

sections.title: Foundations
sections.intro: Eight principles the motion is in service of.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Decide what not to build.

items.title: Agency
items.text: Keep people in control, and make slips easy to undo.

items.title: Responsibility
items.text: Ask only for what you need, and cut a feature whose risk outweighs it.

items.title: Familiarity
items.text: Things that look the same behave the same.

items.title: Flexibility
items.text: Adapt to the device, the situation, and the person.

items.title: Simplicity
items.text: Strip the unnecessary. Show the common path first.

items.title: Craft
items.text: Every spacing, timing, and alignment is a choice you can defend.

items.title: Delight
items.text: The result of the other seven, not something added on top.

sections.title: Reference
sections.intro: The values to reach for first.
items: Start an interrupt from the live transform
Rubber-band an edge instead of a hard stop
